pages.text: Neither melts out of its ore in a furnace. Sphalerite roasts on a fire to zinc oxide, and smithsonite and hemimorphite, the old calamine, calcine to it.
pages.title: Zinc

pages.text: Zinc boils at 907 °C, below the heat that reduces it, so it was distilled from a sealed retort packed with charcoal: a zinc oxide and a charcoal in a basin over a blaze burner fed a blaze cake give a zinc ingot. Asurine, the zinc stone, crushes to smithsonite.

Pentlandite roasts on a fire to a nickel oxide; with a charcoal, superheated, it gives a nickel ingot and the iron goes to slag, and whatever platinum it carried with it. Smelted raw in the bloomery instead, it gives the nickel matte the platinum metals are won from.
pages.title: Nickel

pages.text: Nickel laterite is too lean to roast: four of it with two charcoal, superheated, give one ingot and two slag, as the electric furnaces of Indonesia smelt it whole.
